findings.title: Light-theme username color in embedded posts changed from 30% to 70% lightness
findings.body: In `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a`, the original rule was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new rule is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. The light-theme branch, which should keep the original value, now uses 70% instead of 30%. On the default light theme, the bold username in expanded and in-reply-to posts turns from a dark gray into a pale gray with much lower contrast. The dark branch is also off: it should mirror the original as `$secondary` 70%, not 30%. The rule should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

findings.title: Light/dark lightness values swapped for .custom-message-length
findings.body: The original rule was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, but the replacement is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. Both percentages are inverted. On light themes the flag-message character counter becomes much darker than before. On dark themes it is far brighter than the desktop equivalent in `desktop/modal.scss`, which correctly uses 70%/30%. It should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`.

findings.title: Light-theme color of .group-member-info .name changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: The original `.group-member-info .name` color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. It was replaced with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. This silently lightens group member names on the default light theme and makes `.name` the same color as `.title`, so the two lose their visual distinction. To preserve the light theme and mirror it for dark, use `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

findings.title: Light-theme color of mobile .group-member-info .name changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: This is the same issue as in the desktop stylesheet. The original was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, and it now uses 50% in the light-theme branch, with `$secondary` 50% for dark. On mobile light themes the member name gets lighter and becomes indistinguishable from the title, which is also 50%. It should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

findings.title: Mobile topic-map h3 light-theme color changed from 20% to 50%
findings.body: The original `.topic-map h3` color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`. It was replaced with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. This makes topic-map headings on mobile light themes noticeably lighter. They now match the h4 sub-labels, so the heading/label hierarchy is lost, and they no longer match the desktop rule, which correctly uses 20%/80%. It should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`.

findings.title: Missed conversion: category badge-notification still uses scale-color($primary)
findings.body: `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification` still uses `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)`, even though the same file was otherwise converted. On dark themes, `$primary` is light, so lightening it further by 50% makes these category topic counts nearly white. This is exactly the problem the PR sets out to fix. It should use `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))` like the other rules in this file.
